title: Service Blueprint IR
description: Intermediate representation for a service blueprint, authored as human-editable JSON in the workspace blueprint/ directory and validated by scripts/validate_ir.py (JSON is the supported authoring format; the stdlib scripts read .yaml/.yml only if PyYAML is installed). Mirrors the template data model (see references/data-model.md): service -> phases -> scenarios -> paths -> lanes/steps/cells/dependencies. Every entity carries a stable, locale-independent string key; database UUIDs are UUIDv5-derived from the key path (service/phase/scenario/path/lane/step) plus the locale, NFC-normalized, so re-imports are idempotent by construction. Cells are identified by their (path, lane, step) key triple; dependency edges by their source->target cell pair AND their kind, matching the database's uniqueness key (source_cell_id, target_cell_id, kind). Renaming a key after import creates a NEW identity on the next import. ALL human-readable text fields are locale maps ({en: ..., zh: ...}; additional locales allowed); structural fields (keys, enums, orders, URLs) are locale-independent.

schema_version.description: Template schema version this IR was authored against, newest first — the FIRST entry is the version this template speaks, and validate_ir.py refuses any IR not at it, naming the migration. This enum is the ONE list: scripts/validate_ir.py reads it, and src/lib/backend/schemaVersion.ts is asserted against it. Import performs a compatibility check against the workspace clone's schema_version (see skills/map/references/workspace-state.md) and against a live target's public.schema_version (references/adapter-contract.md § 2). ⚠ Every value added here ships its migration step in scripts/migrate_ir.py in the SAME change — consumers hold signed-off data that cannot be re-derived, so a bump with no step is a bump with no answer (references/customization.md § The versioning rule). A version leaves this list when the migration that carries it forward stops existing. 2026.09.08 was absent for two releases and is the one entry added after the fact: 21000122000000 stamped a database with it for the lane-role vocabulary and taught neither this list nor scripts/migrate_ir.py the value, so a correctly migrated target read as incompatible to scripts/check-target-schema.mjs. The template then added the value and wrote the step that migration never shipped (to_2026_09_08, which renames a lane role carried by its retired spelling). Added, never moved: the stamp sits inside an applied migration and inside the generated portable core, and an applied record keeps the spelling it was written with. 2026.09.10 closes lanes[].role to the eight lanes_lane_role_check has admitted since 21000122000000 — the authoring half of a set that was already closed at import, and the question to_2026_09_08 declined to settle. Its step nulls a role outside the eight, which is what that migration did to every row it found; the database is untouched, so this version stamps no migration and a target at 2026.09.08 stays compatible. 2026.09.11 adds the service's optional `entity_examples` map — the per-kind examples 21000123000000 gave `public.services` and the wire format never learned, so an authored one was dropped on the way to the seed. Nothing authored moves and the database is untouched, so the step is a stamp (to_2026_09_11) and a target at an earlier version stays compatible; the stamp moves at all because a version names a SHAPE, and 2026.09.10 refuses a key this one accepts.

locales.description: Locales this blueprint is authored in. Every localeText field should cover all declared locales; the validator flags gaps. One generated artifact set and one deploy target per locale.

key.description: Stable identifier: lowercase alphanumerics, hyphen, underscore. Locale-independent. Feeds UUIDv5 derivation — treat as permanent once imported.

locale.description: BCP-47-style locale tag, e.g. en, zh, zh-Hant.

localeText.description: Locale -> text map, e.g. {en: 'Submit repair ticket', zh: '提交报修工单'}.

source.description: Source document path or URL this content was extracted from.

section.description: Section heading, page, sheet, or frame within the source.

path.description: The path the cell is on, when it is not the path that lists the link. Absent means that path. Without `scenario`, a path of the same scenario.

scenario.description: The scenario the cell's path is in, when it is not the listing path's scenario. Needs `path`: a scenario holds several paths, so it names none on its own.

cellRef.description: Reference to a cell of this service by its (lane, step) key pair, on the path that lists the link unless `path` (and `scenario`) say otherwise — since 2026.09.12, when a link's reach became one service (ADR 0035). There is no `service` qualifier: the file is one service, and a link may not leave it.

resource.description: Something a cell points at. A link is one kind of resource, which is why the object is named for the parent concept and `kind` carries the subtype.

name.description: What the thing on the other end is called. A NAME, not a title: a reader navigates to it.

url.description: A URI. For an attachment, the file's public URL in Storage — the import never copies bytes, and the database refuses a site-relative path.

kind.description: Subtype. Absent means `link`, a place on the web. `attachment` is a file the cell points at — a site-relative image path, or an object in Storage — and carries a url like a link does. `other` became `attachment` at 2026.09.05; it had named nothing.

featured.description: The resource the cell leads with. One featured attachment per cell (the image it shows); any number of featured links (each a button). Absent means false.

touchpoint.description: One touchpoint used at one cell — the tool, document, channel or artifact the cell's text names. A placement is its words (`summary`), its weight (`role`) and what it points at (`resources`), all belonging to THIS moment: the same tool describes a different screen and points at a different design file at a different step. `screenshots` and `url` became resources on the placement at 2026.09.06 — each screenshot an `attachment` (the first featured), the url a featured `link`. Since 2026.09.07 the name resolves through the service's `touchpoints` registry: a matching entry (case-insensitively) is the placement's touchpoint, and a name the registry lacks is minted into it on import.

name.description: What the touchpoint is called here. Matches a line of the cell's `content` where the grid draws it as a pill; a name that matches nothing still keeps its prose.

summary.description: Long-form copy about this touchpoint at this moment.

role.description: Whether the moment happens THROUGH this touchpoint (core) or the touchpoint is merely present at it (peripheral). On the placement, not the tool: a poster is core at recruitment and incidental three phases later. Absent means nobody has judged this placement, which renders nothing.

resources.description: What this placement points at, in author order: the design file as a featured `link`, screenshots as `attachment`s with the first featured. Read by the cell as its own resources too, through the touchpoint.

entity_examples.description: What each core kind MEANS in this service's own words — one free-text example per kind, keyed by the kind (`service`, `phase`, `scenario`, `path`, `step`, `lane`), shown under that kind's generic definition so a reader is grounded in this deployment rather than the textbook. Lands in `services.entity_examples`. The key set is deliberately NOT an enum here: the kinds are the app's, stated once where the definitions live, and a key the app does not render simply does not render — the same stance the column takes by carrying no CHECK. Optional, and an ABSENT map is not an empty one: a service block that says nothing about examples leaves whatever the deployment has authored in place, because the generated seed cannot tell "nobody wrote any" from "someone deleted them all" and the safe reading of silence is silence. A map that IS present is the whole truth for the service — a kind it omits is cleared on import.

touchpoints.description: The service's touchpoint registry, optional since 2026.09.07. Every placement name across the service becomes a registry row on import whether or not it is listed here; listing one is how it gets a kind, a summary and a home.

loops_to.description: Key of another phase this phase loops back to (loops_to_phase_id).

layout.description: How this scenario opens: stacked = one full band per path on a shared step axis (see paths[].variant_label); merged = the paths combined into one blueprint — one lane rail, one step axis, cells the paths agree on drawn once. Two values since 2026.09.04, which retired `single`: stacked with one path IS one path drawn in full, so `single` only ever changed which component drew it. `merged` had been a session-only display state until the same revision; a scenario left merged now opens merged. 2026.09.03 had retired `side-by-side` and `integrated` into `stacked`.

steps.description: Scenario-scoped step columns, shared across paths. Per-path column order lives in paths[].path_steps.

note.description: Optional note shown with path metadata (e.g. parallel-scenario context).

kind.description: What kind of route this is. Three values since 2026.09.03: `unhappy` and `alternative` were two spellings of the same thing and neither said what it meant, so both became `variant`. `exception` already carries "this went wrong", which is the distinction `unhappy` was reaching for.

variant_label.description: Label for this path as a comparison variant in the stacked layout (e.g. 'as designed' vs 'as actually done'). Any two labeled variants compare — designed-vs-reality is just the default labeling.

path_steps.description: Scenario step keys in column order for THIS path (array index = position). Every cell's step must appear here — the DB trigger aborts imports otherwise.

dependencies.description: Directed dependency edges with at least one end on THIS path; the other end may be on any path of the service, named by its cellRef's `path` (and `scenario`). By convention a link is listed on its source's path and its target is qualified; listing it on both of its paths is a duplicate. Called `triggers` until 2026.09.09: the database has said `cell_dependencies` since 21000103000000 and the domain layer since release 1.5.0, and the interchange format was the estate left over. scripts/migrate_ir.py carries a document authored with the old name across.

display_name.description: Free-form swimlane label in any language (lanes.name in the DB).

role.description: Semantic role key (lanes.lane_role) driving rendering and divider lines. The set is CLOSED at these eight, or null for a generic swimlane — the same set lanes_lane_role_check has admitted since 21000122000000, so a ninth value is refused here while the author can still fix it rather than by a constraint violation part-way through an import. A lane the eight do not name takes null: it draws as a plain swimlane and anchors no divider line, which is exactly how a role outside the set already drew. This enum is a COPY, because JSON Schema cannot import one; scripts/tests/lane-role-roster.test.mjs holds it to the constraint in the generated portable core, to CANONICAL_ROLES in scripts/validate_ir.py and to CANONICAL_LANE_ROLES in src/lib/laneRoles.ts, so the four cannot drift apart again. Adding a ninth role is a deliberate multi-file act — see references/lane-roles.md.

kpis.description: What this lane's actor is measured on (kpi-alignment check reads these).

tools.description: Systems/tools the lane's actor works in (kpi-alignment context).

content.description: Cell label, the primary grid text. Newline-separated items render as pills on pill-role lanes. Omit (or empty strings) for storyboard-row picture cells.

frame.description: The frame: one image on this cell (storyboard rows and illustrated cells). A step's frames across the lanes are its strip.

touchpoints.description: Touchpoints placed at this cell, in author order.

needs_review.description: Low-confidence extraction — surface during review; sign-off should clear or confirm these.

evidence.description: Verbatim quotes or pointers backing this cell (researcher traceability). Reserved shape; no v1 UX.

attribution.description: Who asserted this content (stakeholder-merge conflicts modeled as data). Reserved shape; no v1 UX.

function.description: What this cell does for the journey (spec field; audit wave 2 reads it).

form.description: How the cell manifests — channel, artifact, interface (spec field).

owner.description: Recorded owner tag (shared vocabulary — reuse existing tags).

perceived_owner.description: Who the customer BELIEVES owns this moment (perceived-owner check compares the pair).

kind.description: What kind of dependency this edge is. leads_to: the source makes the target HAPPEN, and the canvas draws an arrow. enables: the source makes the target POSSIBLE without causing it, and the canvas draws nothing — it reads in the cell panel only. Both read source-first and upstream-first, so an edge's direction can be read without checking its kind; the retired `needs` pointed the other way, which is why 2026.09.01 turned those edges around rather than renaming them where they lay. ABSENCE MEANS 'leads_to': that is the cell_dependencies.kind column default and the meaning every edge authored before 2026.08.26 already carried, so a file of bare edges migrates by its stamp alone. The pair alone is no longer an identity — a source->target pair may carry BOTH kinds as two rows, so the UUIDv5 derivation and the duplicate check both read the kind.

dependency.description: Directed dependency edge between two cells of this service — on one path, or on two paths in any scenarios (ADR 0035), never in two services. Identity is the two resolved ends plus the kind, whichever path lists it. source != target, whatever the kind. `kind: leads_to` (the default) is the drawn arrow, and the kind this array held alone when it was called `triggers`; `kind: enables` is the panel-only dependency the database has stored since cell_dependencies grew the column, and which the IR could not express — and therefore silently dropped on export — until 2026.08.26.

registryTouchpoint.description: One entry in the service's touchpoint registry — an app, a document, a channel, a physical thing the service owns. A placement names one of these by name; a placement whose name the registry lacks is minted into it on import, so the registry is where a touchpoint's kind, summary and home live once, not per cell.

name.description: The touchpoint's name, unique within the service (case-insensitively). Placements match it by name.

kind.description: What sort of thing this is. Absent means `other`; never guessed from a name.

summary.description: What this touchpoint IS, for the service — not what it does at any one cell.

url.description: Where the touchpoint itself lives, when it has a home.
